Glossary

Website backup: what is it, and why do it?

A website backup is a copy of all its files and its database, stored somewhere else. If the site breaks, is hacked or a change goes wrong, it is restored to the state of the copy.

The definition in one sentence

It is the site's spare wheel. You hardly ever use it, but on the day you need it, nothing can replace it.

A full backup contains two things:

  • The files: the software, the theme, the extensions, the images.
  • The database: the texts, the pages, the settings, and for a shop, the products and orders.

What it does for a small business

There is no shortage of things that can go wrong: an update that fails, a slip of the hand, a hack, an outage at the web host. With a recent backup, you can go back quickly. Without one, you sometimes have to start again from scratch.

A real-life example

A delicatessen deletes by mistake the page for its gift hampers, the most visited one before Christmas. No panic: the previous day's backup brings it back exactly as it was, with its photos and prices. Without a copy, everything would have had to be rewritten in the middle of the busy season.

The rules of a good backup

  • Regular. The more often the site changes, the more often you need to back it up. A shop taking orders every day needs more frequent copies than a showcase website.
  • Automatic. A backup that relies on someone's memory ends up forgotten.
  • Stored elsewhere. A copy kept on the same server as the site disappears with it if something serious happens.
  • Several versions. If the problem goes back several days, yesterday's copy is already affected. You need to be able to go further back.
  • Tested. A backup you have never tried to restore is just a promise.

Always make a backup just before a big change or a major update. It is the habit that saves the most cold sweats.

Common mistakes

  • Assuming the web host always takes care of it. Not every offer does.
  • Keeping a single copy, overwritten every night.
  • Forgetting the database and only backing up the files.

Backups are part of the upkeep included in the subscription. I take care of them for you, and use them if something needs putting back. You have nothing to schedule. For the rest of the upkeep, see the page on website maintenance.

Your questions

How long should backups be kept?

Long enough to go back to before a problem that went unnoticed for a few days. Keeping several copies of different ages is safer than a single very recent one.

Can I get a copy of my site?

Yes. Your site belongs to you: if you change provider, I hand over its files.
